direction: Evolve the single hook `score_ruin_nodes` into a rank-power multiplicative gating rule that (a) ranks customers by normalized removal savings, (b) multiplies by capacity-tightness and depot-eccentricity gates, and (c) anneals the rank power p with `iter_frac` and `stagnation_ratio` so early iterations remove top-cost nodes and stagnating iterations broaden toward randomized mid-rank removal (diversification). Targets the measured weak regimes of dev_24: capacity_level=tight, depot_style=eccentric, size=100 (uniform demand, clustered spatial).

operations.mechanism: KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the exact template/interface (score_ruin_nodes with fixed deterministic Regret-2 reinsertion, intra_2opt perturbation, R2R acceptance) and its isolated-hook attribution: an evolved rank-power + multiplicative-gate ruin rule beat the zero-evolution Worst-Cost-Removal control (23.3186 vs 23.3474 blind-120 @500 ms) and beat the round-1 constructor+relocate champion on 8/24 dev instances, showing genuine per-instance complementarity rather than skeleton credit. The same entry warns that the hook's sizeable LNS payoff requires ample per-iteration margin; dev_24 means here are 120.6 ms mean vs a 500 ms budget, so there is ~4x headroom and no exhaustion/failure instances were recorded in any regime, letting us safely spend iterations on a richer gated-removal policy. Shaw-regret relatedness and Regret-k insertion entries justify keeping reinsertion deterministic (unchanged, non-evolvable) and only spending evolution budget on the removal-priority signal. The archive shows a single solver with zero VBS gap spread, so any gain must come from improving the one policy; the weakest regimes (tight capacity, eccentric depot, n=100) are exactly where removal geometry matters most (long depot legs + binding load constraints), motivating the load/depot gates and stagnation-annealed rank power.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: For cvrp_ruin_recreate at a 500 ms budget on cvrp_dev_hetero_24, a score_ruin_nodes hook of the form score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i|/scale, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)) * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist (with p decreasing from ~3 toward ~1 as stagnation_ratio grows) will reduce mean tour length by >=1.0% vs the round-1 incumbent (15.7584), and the gain will concentrate in the tight-capacity / eccentric-depot / n=100 regimes where the round-1 VBS relative gap is worst (-23.4%, -21.2%, -22.2%).
